chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Shu'ayb ibn Ya'qub, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about salat (prayer) in saline marshland: why do you dislike it? He said, “Because the forehead does not come to rest evenly.” So I said: if there is level ground in it? He said, “There is no harm.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: There is no harm in performing salat (prayer) in churches and synagogues if the Muslim person faces his qiblah. And salat (prayer) is not performed in the houses of the Magians until they are sprinkled with water.

key_terms.بُيُوتِ ٱلْمَجُوسِ: the houses of the Magians, where sprinkling with water is required before prayer
key_terms.قِبْلَتِهِ: his qiblah, the direction one must face in prayer
key_terms.مُسْتَوِيَةً: level or even, describing the required surface for prostration
key_terms.ٱلسَّبَخَةِ: saline or marshy ground where prayer may be disliked
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship being discussed
key_terms.ٱلْبِيَعِ: churches or places of non-Muslim worship
key_terms.ٱلْجَبْهَةَ: the forehead, whose proper placement in sajdah is legally relevant
key_terms.ٱلْكَنَائِسِ: synagogues or churches, mentioned as permissible places for prayer

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray on saline ground, in churches, or in the houses of the Magians?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal ruling concerning valid places for salat (prayer), focusing on the requirement that the place of prostration be level so that the forehead can rest properly. It also states that salat (prayer) in churches and synagogues is permissible when facing the qiblah, while prayer in the houses of the Magians requires sprinkling water first.
